claims.explanation: Fluspirilene is a diphenylbutylpiperidine that blocks voltage-gated calcium channels and dopamine receptors, and its anticancer activity has been linked to CDK2 inhibition and autophagy induction. Sensitivity is strongly associated with TP53 mutation, which may impair DNA damage responses and autophagy regulation, while intact PTEN/PIK3CA signaling and certain lineage contexts (e.g., colorectal, glioma) appear protective. The drug's known calcium channel antagonism suggests that tumors relying on calcium-dependent survival or autophagy pathways are more vulnerable.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines; p53 loss may impair autophagy and DNA damage responses, enhancing fluspirilene-induced death.
PTEN mutations are more common in resistant lines; intact PTEN may promote survival through PI3K/AKT signaling.
PIK3CA mutations appear in several resistant lines, suggesting activated PI3K signaling reduces sensitivity.
KRAS mutations are frequent in resistant colorectal and pancreatic lines, possibly driving survival pathways.
CDKN2A mutations are seen in multiple sensitive lines, potentially linking cell cycle deregulation to CDK2 inhibition by fluspirilene.
Fluspirilene blocks voltage-gated calcium channels; high expression of CACNA1C (L-type) may increase dependence on calcium signaling.
Fluspirilene inhibits N-type calcium channels; tumors expressing CACNA1B may be more sensitive to channel blockade.
Fluspirilene is a dopamine D2 receptor antagonist; expression of DRD2 may mediate direct antiproliferative effects.
Fluspirilene induces autophagy by preventing calpain1-mediated ATG5 cleavage; high ATG5 levels may enhance autophagy-dependent death.
Calpain1 cleaves ATG5; high calpain1 activity may reduce full-length ATG5 and limit fluspirilene-induced autophagy.
Fluspirilene was identified as a CDK2 inhibitor; high CDK2 expression may predict sensitivity.
NF2 mutations appear in several sensitive lines (SNU840, NCIH2052, BICR6), possibly through Hippo pathway dysregulation.
